solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl is to live very short time

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
in a trice means in a very short time: a trice

explanation.surface: Someone muses on living for only the briefest moment.
explanation.walkthrough: BE plus A TRICE; the article A belongs inside 'very short time', a trice.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, best known from Dante's muse and Shakespeare's heroine in Much Ado.

clue.text: Plant is fine further down

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
lower means further down

explanation.surface: A gardener says a plant does well planted deeper in the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Any bloom-bearing vegetation is a kind of plant, so the general term covers it.

clue.text: Sort of account for nervous anticipation

definitions.meaning: a ... account is a temporary book-keeping entry for unallocated sums
the tense state of waiting to learn an outcome

explanation.definitionFit: Accountants hold unresolved items in a suspense account; separately, the word names tense waiting.

clue.text: Change, putting feet up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for feet is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: paws are an animal's feet

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes by changing position and putting their feet up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PAWS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange one thing for another is a synonym of change.

clue.text: Notes day is stormy: keep calm!

indicators.note: a stormy thing is turbulent, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A weather note warns of a stormy day, with advice not to panic.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation urging someone to restrain themselves, idiomatically equal to telling them not to get excited.

clue.text: Puzzle in game resolved

indicators.note: resolved suggests breaking down and reforming, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A puzzle within a game is finally solved.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery or riddle that baffles is a synonym of puzzle.

clue.text: Tin one penny? A bargain

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether a tin costs one penny, what a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage for a cheap buy, something at a cut price.

clue.text: Shout in pain, being cowardly

parts.note: to yell is to shout
ow is the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: Someone screams when hurt, revealing a lack of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking courage is described with this colour word informally.

clue.text: In time, I lag dreadfully: a restriction on the old?

indicators.note: doing something dreadfully means doing it badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An elderly person laments falling badly behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' rearranges TIMEILAG. The question mark flags that such restrictions usually bar the young.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule barring people above or below a certain years-count is a restriction based on years.

clue.text: Cook's agitated state

definitions.meaning: being in a ... means being anxious and flustered

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means simmering food slowly; the noun also names a flustered, worried condition.

clue.text: Taking only starter in dinner, I am faint

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, so only that opening letter is taken

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A diner eats only the first course and feels weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only starter in' takes D from dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A light or sound that is weak or indistinct can be described with this word.

clue.text: Two drinks before my card game

parts.note: gin is one spirit and rum another, giving the pair of drinks

explanation.surface: Someone has a couple of drinks before playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-player game of melds played with playing cards.

clue.text: Features space to grow fast

parts.note: mush is British slang for the face, one's features
room means space

explanation.surface: Someone's face gives their looks space to develop quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSH is old British slang for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungi spring up overnight, so the verb means to expand rapidly.

clue.text: Married in a church, one's high point

indicators.note: in means the letter for married goes inside the other letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A wedding in church is the best moment of one's life.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or summit of achievement is a synonym of high point.

clue.text: People add up in their heads

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, matching the adverb

parts.note: men are people
to tally is to add up

explanation.surface: People do mental arithmetic without paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Done within the mind is an adverbial sense matching doing sums without pen or paper.

clue.text: Look around in centre of castle

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: to peek is to look

explanation.surface: A tourist looks about in the middle of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The central tower or stronghold of a medieval fortress is called by this term.

clue.text: But such a school is private

definitions.text: But such a school is private

parts.words: But such a school is private
parts.note: in Britain a ... school is a fee-paying independent school, paradoxically private

explanation.surface: A paradox: a certain school called open is in fact private.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, 'public schools' such as Eton are fee-paying private schools.
explanation.definitionFit: British paradox: elite fee-paying establishments carry the opposite-sounding label.

clue.text: Community entertainment regularly rising and falling

definitions.meaning: a gathering where everyone joins in singing
describing a voice with a lilting, monotonous rhythm

explanation.definitionFit: A group sing-along is one sense; the other describes a lilting intonation that rises and falls.

clue.text: Son to go on all fours, showing bad hand

parts.note: to crawl is to move on hands and knees

explanation.surface: A son crawling about displays poor penmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Messy, careless handwriting; hand is a term for writing style.

clue.text: We're disgusted — and some shrug helplessly

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: People are disgusted and shrug, feeling helpless.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation expressing revulsion, the sound a disgusted person makes.

clue.text: Persistently question origin of meat eaten by dog

indicators.note: eaten by means the letter goes inside the word for the dog

parts.note: a pup is a young dog

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dog eats the start of some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin of' takes M from meat; 'eaten by' puts it inside PUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to quiz them hard for information.

clue.text: Soon a refusal from Paris

parts.note: non is French for no

explanation.surface: A Parisian gives a quick refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning shortly or presently.

clue.text: The genuine side of Madrid?

definitions.meaning: ... Madrid is a famous Spanish football team

explanation.definitionFit: Authentic is a synonym; separately, it is the name of the famous Madrid football club.

clue.text: No more room on satellite? It happens every month

definitions.meaning: playfully, the moon being full of people
the lunar phase recurring roughly monthly

explanation.definitionFit: The lunar phase when the whole disc is lit recurs monthly; whimsically, the satellite has no space left.

clue.text: Assassin was old lunatic

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A killer was a crazed old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunatic' rearranges WASOLD. Lee Harvey Oswald shot President Kennedy in 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Harvey Oswald was the killer of President Kennedy.

clue.text: Long-distance traveller, singular fast bowler

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a paceman is a fast bowler in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer who bowls quickly travels far.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a paceman is a fast bowler, who delivers the ball at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut journeys enormous distances off Earth.
